messages.author: bacb0402e67daa77
messages.subject: Fitting Bivariate Data
parts:
Hey Guys,

Still very new to Stan/programming/statistics in general, so I'm building my mental map in regards to how everything works.

I am trying to fit the results of an output of diffeqs solved via the Euler method to two vectors of data, which I will call u1array and u2array.

A simplified pseudocode of the model, where c1 and c2 are parameters.:

I = linspace(0,1,11)
dt = 0.1
ttotal = 1000
eulersteps = int(ttotal/dt)
u1hatarray = []
u2hatarray = []
for I1 in I
    for I2 in I
        for i in 1:eulersteps
            V1 += dt * (c1 * I1 + c2 * I2)
            V2 += dt * (c1 * I2 + c2 * I1)
        u1hatarray.append(V1)
        u2hatarray.append(V2)
 
Now, would it be possible to fit u1hatarray and u2hatarray to u1array and u2array? All the examples I've come across so far have depicted fitting single data vectors?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fitting Bivariate Data
parts:
Yes, you can do what you want in Stan, but you'll have
to code it in Stan's syntax.

For multivariate normal, you ideally want to parameterize
in terms of Cholesky factors and use multi_normal_cholesky
or for 2D, just build the covariance matrix out of two scales
and a correlation.

There are lots of examples in the regression chapter of the manual.
And in the ODE chapter --- we have a built-in ODE solver.

- Bob

The built-in solver should be better than the Euler method
for both accuracy and efficiency.

It's not a stiff solver, though. But then neither is Euler.
